objective: Prove exact triple affine transport, three-port matching gluing, and the conditional absence of cyclic three-edge cuts, with an explicit four-terminal boundary.

atomic_claims.text: Ordered target triples can be affinely matched by edges iff no positional pair is equal on one side and adjacent on the other.
Three distinct low-degree ports can receive distinct labels unless all three independent-port lists are the same nonadjacent pair.
Two B-colorable pieces with three distinct ports of internal degree at most two can be joined by any three-edge matching.
A vertex-minimum triangle-free subcubic non-B-mappable graph has no edge cut of size at most three separating cyclic sides.
The constant four-tuple and (0,12,13,23) pass every triple projection but cannot be affinely edge-matched.

assumptions: Use C06-C07 target generator identities, affine symmetries and exact triple common-neighbor facts.
Port vertices on each side are physically distinct and have internal degree at most two.
Minimality is over all triangle-free subcubic graphs; no assumption that this minimum is cubic.
risks: Paper classification only, no executable enumeration or kernel check.
A fixed incompatible pair of triples may require port relabeling; the gluing proof explicitly supplies it.
The statement does not extend verbatim to four or five terminals.
C12 completion has not been shown to preserve cyclic connectivity.
